items.title: Indian stocks set for pullback after sharp rally on oil slide, foreign inflows
items.description: Indian markets are likely to experience a decline on Friday following a global market selloff. Investor concerns are rising due to the impact of the US Democratic win on regulations and foreign policy. Both Nifty 50 and BSE Sensex ended their six-session winning streak on Thursday. Foreign institutional investors made substantial stock purchases amid shifting market dynamics related to AI.

items.title: Positive Breakout: These 8 large-cap stocks cross above their 200 DMAs
items.description: In the NSE large-cap pack, eight stocks' closing prices crossed above their 200-day moving averages (DMA) on November 5, 2026, according to StockEdge's technical scan data. The 200-day moving average (DMA) is used by traders as a key indicator for determining the overall trend of a stock. As long as a stock's price remains above its 200-day moving average on the daily timeframe, it is generally interpreted as being in an overall uptrend.

items.title: Microfinance lenders tread cautiously amid rural stress
items.description: The microfinance sector experienced varied performance in the second quarter of FY27, reflecting economic uncertainty. Bandhan Bank and CreditAccess Grameen saw declines in their microfinance portfolios, while IndusInd Bank grew its portfolio. Lenders are concerned about the impact of drought and inflation on rural borrowers. Estimates for the sector's growth varied between credit information companies, indicating inconsistencies. Collection discipline has improved, but localized climate disruptions continue to pose risks.

items.title: Sensex stages biggest rally since April as FIIs turn aggressive buyers
items.description: Foreign institutional investors significantly increased their purchases of Indian stocks, leading to substantial market gains. The BSE Sensex rose by 2,008.61 points, achieving its biggest jump since April. Easing crude oil prices contributed to reduced inflation expectations and improved India's macroeconomic outlook. Positive global cues, including gains in US markets, further supported investor sentiment and market performance.

items.title: Sebi eases accreditation norms for AIF, SIF and PMS investors
items.description: The Securities and Exchange Board of India has introduced a new regulation allowing alternative investment fund managers to handle investor accreditation. This initiative is designed to streamline the accreditation process for investors looking for investment options. Managers are now authorized to evaluate eligibility during onboarding or at any stage of the scheme, providing greater flexibility.

items.title: Sebi relaxes cash market settlement rules for mutual funds
items.description: Securities and Exchange Board of India has permitted mutual fund schemes to net fund obligations. This new regulation is set to come into effect starting April 1, 2027. It allows net settlement of funds at the individual scheme level while maintaining gross settlement for securities. Fund obligations cannot be adjusted across different schemes, and inter-scheme funding remains prohibited. Proceeds from outright sales must be funded separately for non-outright obligations.

items.title: FIIs turn buyers in IT, telecom stocks in second half of October ahead of Diwali
items.description: Technology stocks in India are seeing increased interest from foreign institutional investors as Diwali approaches. After struggling in the first half of October, the IT and telecom sectors have gained attention. Foreign portfolio investors made significant net purchases of Indian equities in late October. This upward trend follows substantial selling earlier in the month. The shift highlights a renewed focus on technology investments within the Indian market.

items.title: D-Street braces for gap-down opening on negative GIFT Nifty cues
items.description: On Thursday, the Nifty index exceeded 24,000 for the first time in nearly two months. This rise was supported by falling crude oil prices and substantial foreign institutional investments. Analysts expect Indian equities to maintain a positive trend as the festive season approaches. The rupee also appreciated slightly against the US dollar due to robust foreign fund inflows. Overall, the market outlook remains optimistic despite fluctuating conditions.

items.title: Stocks in news: Bharti Airtel, LIC, Titan, ONGC, Bharti Hexacom, Glenmark Pharma and Astral
items.description: Indian equity markets continued their upward trend, highlighted by the Nifty 50 gaining 576 points. Bharti Airtel, LIC, and Titan Company reported strong profit increases for the September quarter. ONGC also posted a substantial rise in consolidated profit compared to last year. In contrast, Glenmark Pharmaceuticals faced a significant decline in net profit this quarter. Overall, corporate developments are influencing investor sentiment as markets react to earnings reports.

items.title: M-cap of BSE-listed companies tops Rs 500 lakh crore mark
items.description: The BSE has hit a significant milestone as the collective market capitalization of listed firms exceeded ₹500 lakh crore, driven by a comprehensive market rally and new listings. Although many indices remain below their historical peaks, strong demand from foreign portfolio investors and favorable global signals have led to an uplift in market sentiment. Challenges such as geopolitical shifts and profit booking, however, could threaten future expansion.

items.title: Demat account additions hit 9-month high in October as IPO boom draws investors
items.description: In October 2026, new demat account additions reached a nine-month high, driven by strong IPO activity. NSDL and CDSL reported adding nearly 3.36 million accounts during the month. The total number of demat accounts at the end of October was approximately 244 million. The increase in account openings was mainly influenced by the successful launch of several public issues.

items.title: Stock Radar: Coforge stock hits fresh record high in November 2026; will the rally continue?
items.description: Coforge Ltd has successfully broken out of a lengthy consolidation phase that lasted over two months. The stock now shows potential targets above the 2,200 levels in the upcoming weeks. Key support levels are established, with immediate support at 1,940 and previous resistance around 2,000. Experts suggest maintaining strategic stop losses to manage potential downside risks effectively. Momentum indicators favor continued bullish trends, indicating further growth opportunities for traders.

items.title: Gold loan NPA rises in first five months while eases over a three-year horizon
items.description: India’s gold loan market has experienced a rise in non-performing assets, reaching 0.78% by August 2023. The total outstanding volume grew nearly threefold to Rs 22.5 lakh crore recently. Borrowers are increasingly taking multiple loans, with many having four or more gold loans. The market also saw 5.5 crore active borrowers, indicating its broad consumer reach.

items.title: MobiKwik shares jump 4% as RBI approves NBFC licence; co targets Rs 5,000 crore loans
items.description: MobiKwik shares gained on Friday after the RBI granted its subsidiary a licence to operate as an NBFC, enabling the fintech company to enter direct lending. MobiKwik plans to disburse Rs 5,000 crore in loans over the next three to four years, targeting consumers and MSMEs through secured and unsecured products.

items.title: 12 midcap stocks deliver returns of up to 136% in FY27 so far
items.description: The broader market rally has been particularly strong in the midcap segment in FY27 so far. While the benchmark Nifty50 has gained around 10%, the Nifty Midcap 150 index has outperformed with a nearly 15% rise. The rally has also translated into sharp gains for several individual stocks, with around 42 midcap stocks advancing more than 25% during this period.Among these, we highlight 12 stocks that have delivered impressive returns, surging between 50% and 136% so far in FY27. (Data Source: ACE Equity)

items.title: Angel One edges past Zerodha in NSE active investors, claims second spot; Groww leads
items.description: Angel One has overtaken Zerodha to become India's second-largest stockbroker by active NSE investors, adding 2.43 lakh investors in October. Groww retained the top position with 1.37 crore active investors. Angel One also reported its highest monthly client additions in nine months, alongside an improvement in trading activity and market share.

items.title: These large-, mid- and small-cap stocks have upside potential of up to 31% in 1 year, according to analysts
items.description: In the last two years, the world has learnt that you can never quite predict what US President Trump will do next. Tomorrow, to pull attention one way or another, there could well be some more action against Iran, changing the mood again in a single afternoon. So, the improvement in sentiment is real, but it is also fragile.

items.title: Honasa Consumer Q2 Results: Mamaearth parent's profit surges 87% YoY to Rs 73 crore
items.description: Honasa Consumer achieved an 86.7% increase in net profit for the September quarter, reaching Rs 73.25 crore. Revenue from operations grew by 35.9% compared to the previous year, amounting to Rs 731.19 crore. Despite sequential profit decline, the company indicated strong performance across various sales channels, including general and modern trade. The flagship brand Mamaearth continued to show robust growth, contributing significantly to overall earnings.

items.title: Nifty’s 8% surge this week is the best since January 2021. Are bulls here to stay?
items.description: Nifty surged 8% this week, marking its biggest weekly gain since January 2021, as foreign investors returned to Indian equities. Strong Q2 earnings, attractive valuations and a global shift away from AI-linked stocks supported the rally. The key question now is whether renewed buying can sustain the market's recovery.

items.title: $5 billion in 5 days! Why FIIs are suddenly shopping Indian stocks non-stop this Diwali
items.description: Foreign institutional investors have poured nearly $5 billion into Indian equities in five trading sessions, marking a sharp reversal after months of heavy selling. Strong Q2 earnings, softer crude prices, stable currency and the global AI sell-off are improving India's appeal, with investors rotating towards relatively undervalued markets and large-cap stocks.

items.title: Groww shares decline 7% after Rs 3,708 crore block deal involving 2.8% equity
items.description: Shares of Groww parent Billionbrains Garage Ventures fell on Friday after a block deal involving 17.42 crore shares, or 2.8% of the company's equity, worth around Rs 3,708 crore was executed at an average price of Rs 215 apiece. The buyers and sellers were not immediately identified. The decline followed a sharp rally in the previous session, when the stock touched Rs 225.75, and may indicate profit-booking.

items.title: Kalyan, Titan, other Jewellery stocks rally up to 5% on Dhanteras 2026. How is yellow metal placed this festive season?
items.description: Jewellery stocks rallied ahead of Dhanteras 2026 as investors anticipated stronger precious metal demand. Meanwhile, brokerages see opportunities in gold and silver following their recent corrections, with Axis Securities and Religare Broking outlining accumulation ranges, price targets and key support levels.

items.title: India’s new wealth rituals: What are millennials and Gen Z buying on Dhanteras?
items.description: Dhanteras investing is evolving from physical gold purchases toward diversified digital portfolios. Younger investors are embracing gold ETFs, mutual funds, Bitcoin and tokenised assets while retaining the festival’s core goal of building wealth and financial security patiently.

items.title: Beyond gold: What $340 billion in crypto flows says about India's investment preferences this Dhanteras
items.description: Gold remains central to Indian household savings, but high prices are pushing investors toward ETFs and digital gold instead of physical holdings. Crypto is emerging as a separate portfolio option rather than replacing gold, reflecting a broader shift toward digital ownership and diversification.

items.title: Sai Life Sciences shares rally 9% after Q2 results; net profit rises 17%, revenue up 23%
items.description: Sai Life Sciences shares jumped nearly 9% to a fresh 52-week high after strong second-quarter results. Revenue rose 23%, while net profit increased 17%, supported by sustained business momentum and growing engagement with global pharmaceutical companies.

items.title: Nomura silences AI doubters, says Kospi can hit 10,000 mark to double as fundamentals are intact
items.description: South Korea's Kospi plunged to a nine-month low amid fears that US political shifts could slow AI infrastructure spending and hurt chip demand. However, Nomura remains bullish, projecting a potential recovery towards 10,000, with a near-term target of 7,500–8,000.

items.title: Largecap dhamaka! 6 bluechip stocks with upside of up to 48% to buy this Diwali
items.description: As investors enter Samvat 2083, the landscape calls for selectivity rather than indiscriminate optimism. Global uncertainties, fluctuating capital flows and evolving market expectations continue to influence equity performance. In this environment, sustainable wealth creation is likely to depend less on broad-based market movements and more on identifying businesses capable of delivering consistent earnings growth. Here are 10 largecap stocks Religare is bullish on.

items.title: Mahindra & Mahindra shares gain 3% after Q2 profit jumps 25% to Rs 4,588 crore, revenue grows 25%
items.description: Mahindra & Mahindra shares rose after the company reported a 25% year-on-year jump in consolidated Q2 net profit to Rs 4,588 crore. Revenue also grew 25.4% to Rs 57,515 crore. Total expenses increased 25.9% to Rs 51,845 crore.

items.title: Stock Market Holiday 2026: When will BSE & NSE be closed for Diwali? Muhurat trading timings, other key things to know
items.description: Indian stock markets will hold a special Muhurat Trading session on Sunday, November 8, to mark Diwali, despite the regular trading holiday. BSE and NSE will remain shut on November 10 for Diwali-Balipratipada. Check the complete schedule and timings.
